segs.e: Linked Discourses 13.1
1. Comprehension
A Fingernail
So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

segs.p: Atha kho bhagavā parittaṁ nakhasikhāyaṁ paṁsuṁ āropetvā bhikkhū āmantesi:
segs.e: Then the Buddha, picking up a little bit of dirt on his fingernail, addressed the mendicants:
“What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: katamaṁ nu kho bahutaraṁ, yo vāyaṁ mayā paritto nakhasikhāyaṁ paṁsu āropito, ayaṁ vā mahāpathavī”ti?
segs.e: Which is more: the little bit of dirt on my fingernail, or this great earth?”
“Sir, the great earth is far more.

segs.p: Appamattako bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṁ paṁsu āropito.
segs.e: The little bit of dirt on your fingernail is tiny.

segs.p: Neva satimaṁ kalaṁ upeti na sahassimaṁ kalaṁ upeti na satasahassimaṁ kalaṁ upeti mahāpathaviṁ upanidhāya bhagavatā paritto nakhasikhāyaṁ paṁsu āropito”ti.
segs.e: Compared to the great earth, it’s not nearly a hundredth, a thousandth, or a hundred thousandth part.”

segs.p: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa abhisametāvino etadeva bahutaraṁ dukkhaṁ yadidaṁ parikkhīṇaṁ pariyādiṇṇaṁ;
segs.e: “In the same way, for a noble disciple accomplished in view, an individual with comprehension, the suffering that’s over and done with is more,
what’s left is tiny.

segs.p: Neva satimaṁ kalaṁ upeti na sahassimaṁ kalaṁ upeti na satasahassimaṁ kalaṁ upeti purimaṁ dukkhakkhandhaṁ parikkhīṇaṁ pariyādiṇṇaṁ upanidhāya yadidaṁ sattakkhattuṁparamatā.
segs.e: Compared to the mass of suffering in the past that’s over and done with, it’s not nearly a hundredth, a thousandth, or a hundred thousandth part, since there are at most seven more lives.
That’s how very beneficial it is to comprehend the teaching
and gain the vision of the teaching.”
Linked Discourses 13.2
1. Comprehension
A Lotus Pond
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, pokkharaṇī paññāsayojanāni āyāmena paññāsayojanāni vitthārena paññāsayojanāni ubbedhena, puṇṇā udakassa samatittikā kākapeyyā.
segs.e: “Mendicants, suppose there was a lotus pond that was fifty leagues long, fifty leagues wide, and fifty leagues deep, full to the brim so a crow could drink from it.
Then a person would pick up some water on the tip of a blade of grass.
What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: katamaṁ nu kho bahutaraṁ, yaṁ vā kusaggena udakaṁ ubbhataṁ yaṁ vā pokkharaṇiyā udakan”ti?
segs.e: Which is more: the water on the tip of the blade of grass, or the water in the lotus pond?”
“Sir, the water in the lotus pond is certainly more.
The water on the tip of a blade of grass is tiny.

segs.p: Neva satimaṁ kalaṁ upeti na sahassimaṁ kalaṁ upeti na satasahassimaṁ kalaṁ upeti pokkharaṇiyā udakaṁ upanidhāya kusaggena udakaṁ ubbhatan”ti.
segs.e: Compared to the water in the lotus pond, it’s not nearly a hundredth, a thousandth, or a hundred thousandth part.”

segs.p: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa abhisametāvino etadeva bahutaraṁ dukkhaṁ yadidaṁ parikkhīṇaṁ pariyādiṇṇaṁ; appamattakaṁ avasiṭṭhaṁ.
segs.e: “In the same way, for an individual with comprehension, a noble disciple accomplished in view, the suffering that’s over and done with is more, what’s left is tiny.

segs.p: Neva satimaṁ kalaṁ upeti na sahassimaṁ kalaṁ upeti na satasahassimaṁ kalaṁ upeti purimaṁ dukkhakkhandhaṁ parikkhīṇaṁ pariyādiṇṇaṁ upanidhāya, yadidaṁ sattakkhattuṁparamatā.
segs.e: Compared to the mass of suffering in the past that’s over and done with, it’s not nearly a hundredth, a thousandth, or a hundred thousandth part, since there are at most seven more lives.

segs.p: Evaṁ mahatthiyo kho, bhikkhave, dhammābhisamayo; evaṁ mahatthiyo dhammacakkhupaṭilābho”ti.
segs.e: That’s how very beneficial it is to comprehend the teaching and gain the vision of the teaching.”
Linked Discourses 13.3
1. Comprehension
Where the Waters Join Together
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yatthimā mahānadiyo saṁsandanti samenti, seyyathidaṁ—
segs.e: “Mendicants, there are places where the great rivers—the Ganges, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī—join together and converge.

segs.p: gaṅgā yamunā aciravatī sarabhū mahī, tato puriso dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni uddhareyya.
segs.e: Suppose a person was to draw two or three drops of water from such a place.
What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: katamaṁ nu kho bahutaraṁ, yāni vā dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni ubbhatāni yaṁ vā sambhejjaudakan”ti?
segs.e: Which is more: the two or three drops drawn out or the water in the confluence?”
“Sir, the water in the confluence is certainly more.

segs.p: appamattakāni dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni ubbhatāni.
segs.e: The two or three drops drawn out are tiny.

segs.p: Neva satimaṁ kalaṁ upenti na sahassimaṁ kalaṁ upenti na satasahassimaṁ kalaṁ upenti sambhejjaudakaṁ upanidhāya dve vā tīṇi vā udakaphusitāni ubbhatānī”ti.
segs.e: Compared to the water in the confluence, it’s not nearly a hundredth, a thousandth, or a hundred thousandth part.”
“In the same way, for a noble disciple, the suffering that’s over and done with is more …”

Linked Discourses 13.5
1. Comprehension
The Earth
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso mahāpathaviyā satta kolaṭṭhimattiyo guḷikā upanikkhipeyya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, suppose a person was to place seven clay balls the size of jujube seeds on the great earth.
What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: katamaṁ nu kho bahutaraṁ, yā vā satta kolaṭṭhimattiyo guḷikā upanikkhittā yā vā mahāpathavī”ti?

“Sir, the great earth is certainly more.

A Mountain
At Sāvatthī.

segs.e: “Mendicants, suppose a person was to place seven pebbles the size of mustard seeds on the Himalayas, the king of mountains.
What do you think, mendicants?

Linked Discourses 13.11
1. Comprehension
A Mountain (3rd)
At Sāvatthī.

segs.p: “Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, puriso sinerussa pabbatarājassa satta muggamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā upanikkhipeyya.
segs.e: “Mendicants, suppose a person was to place on Sineru, the king of mountains, seven pebbles the size of mung beans.
What do you think, mendicants?

segs.p: katamaṁ nu kho bahutaraṁ, yā vā satta muggamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā upanikkhittā yo vā sineru pabbatarājā”ti?
segs.e: Which is more: the seven pebbles the size of mung beans, or Sineru, the king of mountains?”
“Sir, Sineru, the king of mountains, is certainly more.
The seven pebbles the size of mung beans are tiny.

segs.p: Neva satimaṁ kalaṁ upenti na sahassimaṁ kalaṁ upenti na satasahassimaṁ kalaṁ upenti sineruṁ pabbatarājānaṁ upanidhāya satta muggamattiyo pāsāṇasakkharā upanikkhittā”ti.
segs.e: Compared to Sineru, it’s not nearly a hundredth, a thousandth, or a hundred thousandth part.”

segs.p: “Evameva kho, bhikkhave, ariyasāvakassa diṭṭhisampannassa puggalassa adhigamaṁ upanidhāya aññatitthiyasamaṇabrāhmaṇaparibbājakānaṁ adhigamo neva satimaṁ kalaṁ upeti na sahassimaṁ kalaṁ upeti na satasahassimaṁ kalaṁ upeti.
segs.e: “In the same way, compared with the achievements of a noble disciple accomplished in view, the achievements of the ascetics, brahmins, and wanderers of other religions is not nearly a hundredth, a thousandth, or a hundred thousandth part.

segs.p: Evaṁ mahādhigamo, bhikkhave, diṭṭhisampanno puggalo, evaṁ mahābhiñño”ti.
segs.e: So great is the achievement of the individual accomplished in view, so great is their direct knowledge.”
The Linked Discourses on comprehension are complete.
